title: Withholding under correlated reward shocks
subfield: Selfish mining, withholding strategies and attack rationality
open: Derive optimal withholding when exceptional rewards arrive in correlated bursts, decay with delay and differ across private mempools.
status: Research target beyond the 2025 general stochastic-reward framework, adding richer information structures and model uncertainty.
why: Average fees conceal economically important reward timing.
key_works: Bahrani, Neuder and Weinberg (2025), *Selfish Mining under General Stochastic Rewards*, arXiv:2502.20360; Sarenche et al. (2025), *Bitcoin under Volatile Block Rewards: How Mempool Statistics Can Influence Bitcoin Mining*, arXiv:2411.11702.

title: Foreknowledge-free whale-transaction attacks
subfield: Selfish mining, withholding strategies and attack rationality
open: Measure the value of advance transaction information using attack comparisons with identical observable information and no future-arrival leakage.
status: Research target sharpened by 2025 analysis identifying implicit reward predictability in WeRLman’s model.
why: Simulator information leakage can exaggerate attack feasibility.
key_works: Bar-Zur et al. (2023), *WeRLman: To Tackle Whale (Transactions), Go Deep (RL)*, DOI:10.1109/SP46215.2023.10179444; Sarenche et al. (2025), arXiv:2411.11702.

title: Security under abrupt hashpower migration
subfield: Difficulty adjustment, timestamps and consensus clocks
open: Derive tight confirmation guarantees through adversarially timed hashpower changes and retarget boundaries using conservatively observable quantities.
status: Research target extending the 2017 variable-difficulty backbone and 2022 fixed-rate latency bounds.
why: Confirmation counts need meaning during mining shocks.
key_works: Garay, Kiayias and Leonardos (2017), *The Bitcoin Backbone Protocol with Chains of Variable Difficulty*, IACR ePrint:2016/1048; Guo and Ren (2022), *Bitcoin’s Latency–Security Analysis Made Simple*, arXiv:2203.06357.

title: Adaptive GHOSTDAG parameter calibration
subfield: DAG ledgers, fork choice and reward structure
open: Update GHOSTDAG concurrency tolerance from observations without attacker-controlled estimates or unsafe transitions.
status: Research target beyond the 2021 construction; DAG KNIGHT takes a different parameterless approach.
key_works: Sompolinsky, Wyborski and Zohar (2021), *PHANTOM GHOSTDAG: A Scalable Generalization of Nakamoto Consensus*, DOI:10.1145/3479722.3480990; Sutton and Sompolinsky (2023), *The DAG KNIGHT Protocol*, IACR ePrint:2022/1494.

title: Searcher-oracle mechanisms for large transactions
open: Obtain truthful, false-name-resistant welfare guarantees when MEV-informed transactions or bundles consume substantial fractions of block capacity.
status: Research target beyond SAKA’s approximately half-optimal small-transaction guarantee and matching deterministic limitation.
why: Large indivisible bundles violate small-item assumptions.
key_works: Bahrani, Garimidi and Roughgarden (2024), *Transaction Fee Mechanism Design in a Post-MEV World*, DOI:10.4230/LIPIcs.AFT.2024.29.

title: Shared-discount EIP-1559 conjecture
open: Prove or refute near-optimal welfare for modified EIP-1559 with a common transaction discount rate; quantify loss versus capacity slack.
status: Explicit March 2026 conjecture. Fully patient guarantees and heterogeneous-discount impossibilities are established.
why: Extends guarantees to value that decays while waiting.
key_works: Babaioff and Nisan (2025–2026), *On the Welfare of EIP-1559 with Patient Bidders*, arXiv:2502.20031.

title: Efficient selection of fee dimensions
open: Approximate the best small set of fee dimensions for an evolving resource-capacity region, with provable approximation guarantees.
status: Research target after 2025 characterization of one-dimensional approximation and NP-completeness for general optimal dimension selection.
why: Identifies which dimensions justify implementation complexity.
key_works: Lavee et al. (2025), *Does Your Blockchain Need Multidimensional Transaction Fees?*, arXiv:2504.15438.

title: Execution-ticket capital concentration
subfield: PBS market structure, inclusion and builder infrastructure
open: Bound concentration in execution tickets when buyers have unequal financing costs and risk tolerance.
status: Research target since 2024 analysis identified concentration and restrictive conditions for complete MEV capture.
why: Cheap financing can monopolize advance rights.
key_works: Burian, Crapis and Saleh (2024), *MEV Capture and Decentralization in Execution Tickets*, arXiv:2408.11255.

title: Fair-order evidence at validator scale
subfield: Fair ordering, encrypted mempools and transaction privacy
open: Reduce auditable fair-order evidence costs for large changing committees without sacrificing fault tolerance or introducing a trusted coordinator.
status: Research target beyond Quick Order Fairness’s 2022 optimal resilience and quadratic amortized communication.
why: Makes fairness affordable at larger scale.
key_works: Cachin et al. (2022), *Quick Order Fairness*, arXiv:2112.06615.

title: Counterfactual ground truth for MEV detectors
subfield: MEV measurement, benchmarks and research infrastructure
open: Build independently checked traces distinguishing extractable value, realized profit and user harm, including failures and benign lookalikes.
status: Data target extending measurements begun in 2019; counterfactual scope and uncertainty require explicit certification.
why: Avoids evaluating heuristics against their own labels.
key_works: Daian et al. (2019), *Flash Boys 2.0: Frontrunning, Transaction Reordering, and Consensus Instability in Decentralized Exchanges*, arXiv:1904.05234.

title: Joint vault-and-holder peg equilibrium
open: Characterize stability when strategic vaults choose leverage and heterogeneous holders enter, redeem or switch currencies.
status: Research target beyond 2020–2022 stochastic stable and unstable regime results.
why: Replaces fixed-demand peg claims with strategic participation.
key_works: Klages-Mundt and Minca (2022), *While stability lasts: A stochastic model of noncustodial stablecoins*, DOI:10.1111/mafi.12357.

title: Tenfold payment-channel capital efficiency
open: Demonstrate tenfold completed volume per locked coin with comparable safety, latency and churn robustness on published asymmetric workloads.
status: Moonshot building on 2017 rebalancing and 2020 congestion-control routing.
key_works: Sivaraman et al. (2020), [*High Throughput Cryptocurrency Routing in Payment Channel Networks*](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/nsdi20-paper-sivaraman.pdf); Khalil and Gervais (2017), *Revive*, IACR ePrint:2017/823.

title: Fair exchange across heterogeneous finality
open: Extend collusion-resistant exchange to ledgers with unequal rollback and censorship risks, bounding required collateral and outside incentives.
status: Research target beyond Rapidash’s 2022 preprint and FC 2025 user–miner-collusion guarantees.
why: Matches exchange security to actual settlement paths.
key_works: Chung, Masserova, Shi and Thyagarajan (2022; FC 2025), *Rapidash: Atomic Swaps Secure under User-Miner Collusion*, IACR ePrint:2022/1063.

title: Bayesian Sybil reserve prices in proof auctions
subfield: Proof markets, verification incentives and cryptographic mechanisms
open: Characterize distribution-aware fake-user bidding by provers and design auctions bounding the resulting expected gains.
status: Explicit future direction in Prooφ’s 2025 revision.
why: Prevents suppliers from fabricating hidden price floors.
key_works: Wang, Zhou, Yaish, Zhang, Fisch and Livshits (2025), *Prooφ: A ZKP Market Mechanism*, arXiv:2404.06495.

title: Paid verification when fraud is vanishingly rare
subfield: Proof markets, verification incentives and cryptographic mechanisms
open: Sustain independent verification in equilibrium when deterrence makes successful fraud rewards rare, accounting for free riding and outside attackers.
status: Research target since the verifier’s dilemma was articulated in 2015.
why: Maintains an economically credible verification assumption.
key_works: Luu, Teutsch, Kulkarni and Saxena (2015), *Demystifying Incentives in the Consensus Computer*, IACR ePrint:2015/702.

title: Optimal deterministic scheduling with weak discounting
subfield: Online algorithms and formal economic security
open: Determine the optimal deterministic competitive ratio for discounted packet scheduling throughout approximately 0.770018 < λ < 1.
status: Explicitly open in the 2026 revision; smaller-λ bounds match, and the classical undiscounted endpoint is solved.
why: Gives sharp guarantees for financially decaying jobs.
key_works: Gafni and Yaish (2024; revised 2026), *Online Packet Scheduling With Time Discounts*, arXiv:2402.08549.

title: Heterogeneous discounting with batch capacity
subfield: Online algorithms and formal economic security
open: Obtain tight competitive guarantees for differently sized jobs with different decay laws and capacity-constrained batches.
status: Research target beyond the 2024–2026 common-discount unit-service model.
why: Matches actual block and compute-market allocation.
key_works: Gafni and Yaish (2024–2026), *Online Packet Scheduling With Time Discounts*, arXiv:2402.08549.
